content: 1. Strong inducers of the enzyme CYP3A4 can lead to a loss of virologic response and potentially cause resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class of drugs. Close monitoring is required in such cases. 2. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of sunitinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely when these drugs are co-administered. 3. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when combined with drugs that have a known risk of Torsade de Pointes. Close monitoring is essential. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of tacrolimus by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 5. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of telavancin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are used together. 6. Co-administration of tetrabenazine and rilpivirine, both of which prolong the QTc interval, should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. 7. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of thioridazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 8. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of thiothixene by prolonging the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 9. Tipranavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. However, rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. 10. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of toremifene by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 11. Tovorafenib decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of efficacy. 12. Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. If antacids must be used, administer them at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 13. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of trimipramine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 14. Ublituximab decreases the effects of rilpivirine due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 15. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Extreme caution is advised when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 16. Valbenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 17. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vandetanib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 18. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Extreme caution is advised when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 19. Voclosporin and rilpivirine may each increase the effects of the other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 20. Vonoprazan decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Voriconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dose adjustment for rilpivirine is required. However, rilpivirine increases the toxicity of voriconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 23. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ziprasidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 24. In HIV-1-infected pregnant individuals who are virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) and on a stable rilpivirine-containing regimen prior to pregnancy, no dose adjustments are required. However, close monitoring of viral load is necessary, as lower rilpivirine exposures have been observed during pregnancy. 25. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend that HIV-infected mothers should not breastfeed their infants to avoid the risk of postnatal HIV transmission. 26. Emtricitabine (FTC) has been shown to be present in human breast milk. It is unknown if rilpivirine (RPV) and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) are present in human breast milk. However, rilpivirine is present in rat milk, and tenofovir has been detected in the milk of lactating rats and rhesus monkeys. Due to the potential for HIV transmission (in HIV-negative infants), development of viral resistance (in HIV-positive infants), and adverse reactions in breastfed infants similar to those seen in adults, mothers should be instructed not to breastfeed. 27. Rilpivirine is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 28. Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) should be taken with food. Store the medication at temperatures below 30°C (86°F) and keep the container tightly closed. Dispense only in the original container. 29.
